changes.evidence: Team X was Weapon X's Cold War black-ops unit and was disbanded after the Russia mission against Omega Red, all before the original series. The show only depicts it in flashbacks (TAS 'Weapon X, Lies and Videotape'). During TAS Sabretooth works alone or as a hireling for Magneto and Apocalypse. Team X really reforms in X-Men '97 episode 15 (S2E5), when Wolverine recruits Sabretooth, Lady Deathstrike, Maverick and Kane for the Weapon X raid. So the TAS Team X stage, and the TAS departure that follows it, are backstory (the 'left' entry for X-Men: The Animated Series should go as well).

In X-Men '97 episode 13 (S2E3), set in 3000 B.C., En Sabah Nur is a member of Baal's Sandstormers raiders and leads their uprising against Rama-Tut. Rama-Tut's strike kills every Sandstormer except Nur. In episode 14 he breaks with the stranded X-Men and takes the Death Seed to become Apocalypse, and his Horsemen come later. No stage records his Sandstormers membership or the group's end.

After Genosha falls (episode 5), Magneto turns on the X-Men in episode 9 and leads a mutant exodus to Asteroid M. In episode 10 Xavier breaks through to him and he saves the Earth alongside the team. In S2 episodes 13-14 he fights as one of the stranded X-Men (Xavier, Beast, Rogue, Nightcrawler) in ancient Egypt, and Apocalypse kills him there. The Marvel Database lists the X-Men as his current affiliation. His record still ends on Genosha.

In X-Men '97 episode 10, freed by Magneto's blackout, Omega Red guards a Russian government official with Darkstar and Crimson Dynamo, the Winter Guard. The Marvel Database lists the Winter Guard as his affiliation. No stage records this. (The '(from the start)' tag is replaced because there are now two groups.)

In TAS episode 23 ('Beauty and the Beast'), the X-Men expose him as Sabretooth's son, and his men abandon him. He breaks down and is hospitalized. In episode 59 ('Bloodlines') the Friends of Humanity council lets him back in only if he proves himself by killing his mutant family. The ouster and the return are not recorded.

In X-Men '97 episode 5 Exodus lives on Genosha (Genoshan citizen) before the Sentinel massacre. After the massacre the Acolytes reform under his lead (episode 17, S2E7). His Genosha membership on file is not recorded.

owner_calls.question: Is 'Soviet Armed Forces' backstory (B)? He was a Cold War Soviet weapon. In TAS the USSR has already collapsed: rogue former-Soviet generals revive him and he turns on them to rule himself, and later the Russian government thaws him for the submarine job.
options: Keep Soviet Armed Forces at X-Men: The Animated Series
Remove it (backstory), leaving [["The Winter Guard", "X-Men '97 S1"]]
Replace it with Independent for TAS (he defects from the generals in episode 17)
owner_calls.evidence: Marvel Database: created by Soviet generals during the Cold War and frozen. After the Soviet collapse, radical generals free him to reform the union, but he seeks to rule it himself (TAS 'Red Dawn').

owner_calls.question: Does Victor lose Von Doom Industries in Fantastic Four (2005)? His stockholders pull out after the failed mission, and board member Ned Cecil attempts a takeover before Victor kills him. The Marvel Database lists VDI only as a former affiliation, and the company's fate is called unknown. In Rise of the Silver Surfer he works with the US military, not VDI.
owner_calls.evidence: Wikipedia plot: stockholders 'decide to pull out of Von Doom Industries'. Marvel Database VDI page: Victor is a former leader, and it is 'unknown what became of the company following Ned Cecil's death during his attempted takeover and Doom's defeat.'
